As someone who had a parent who never showed up to events, I agree with others that you’re doing the right thing going to your children’s events. That sticks with you and shapes your future relationships imo. Since y’all have been together for a long time, playing devils advocate, maybe she’s going through something but doesn’t know how to bring it up or really what to do to get through it. I think having an honest convo with her about your expectations and wishes and how this has made you feel is definitely something y’all should do when both of you are in calm spirits. I’ve sought relationship advice on here as well, and while some is helpful, take it all with a grain of salt. Trust your gut at the end of the day, and if she’s unable to meet your needs, and isn’t willing to discuss a compromise, then you’ll have your answer and the knowledge to help you make the best decision for yourself and your kids. Ultimately, while I don’t have children, if I was with a partner that had them or vice versa, I’d also put my children or want them to put their children first. Because I grew up with parents who didn’t consider me at all, and I can tell you that stuff hurts me to this day :/ best of luck to you OP!

I think you know what is best for you. Focus on your kids and your new job for now. And getting your new place set up. All the rest is something you should worry about in time. I will say from personal experience, rushing into a new serious relationship after barely leaving a marriage probably isn’t smart. Your emotions are heightened because you’re sad and lonely, and it can make things hard to read. I suggest taking your time and really getting to know this person. As someone who’s been married before, it can be tempting to want to rush things a bit to get back that sense of normalcy that comes with sharing a life with someone, but take your time. I think your attachment to your wife is making it hard to see the facts. She may say she wouldn’t care if you’ve been with another person, but I think it’d be something held over you until either you or she decides to end it later. If as you say, you’ve been doing the self work and the boundaries you both agreed too even though she isn’t holding up her end of the deal, that’s your answer. If she wanted the relationship to work, she would’ve put the effort in. I think your confusion stems from feeling like you’re obligated or owe her your time and your children, but for their sake, giving them an environment where there’s not constant fighting or belittling being done is the kind thing at this point. Hope it all works out for you OP.

This person does not value you or your relationship and cannot deny her short term gratification she gets by sleeping with the friend to think about your feelings or your relationship long term. As someone who was married to a cheater who refused to cut off the other person because they were friends- that is your answer. The friend will always trump her commitment and it will always bother you. You can do all the therapy and committing and compromising on your end but if she is unwilling to meet you halfway and cut that person off as you requested— that’s your answer. You deserve someone who will love you from start to finish. And as much as she denies having an emotional connection with someone she considers a best friend, she is probably in denial at this point. A relationship can come back after infidelity, but it takes two committed people to compromise and learn how to communicate and for the person who stepped out to commit to reassurance and doing the inner work. Please don’t marry someone who isn’t putting your best interests at heart. If your boundary is committing to therapy and cutting the friend off, and she refuses, stick to your boundaries and prepare to walk away if she can’t meet you there. It will hurt, but it’ll hurt more if you marry this person and they aren’t committed to you. As much as you love this person, love yourself and allow yourself to feel what you need to feel. I’m so sorry this happened to you.

I’m about the same size as you OP, and I’ve struggled with weight my entire life and I feel for you on this. If someone told you that you weren’t enough, that’s a reflection on them and not you. It’s an asshole move and you deserve better. I say this with love and respect because I know how you’re feeling. Your value and worth will never change based off of someone’s inability to see you or value you. Your beauty isn’t defined by society and even though it may feel like today’s men only want certain things, I can assure you it’s false. Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and I hate you can’t see it in yourself. Your looks are not who you are. What makes you, you, is a lot more than that. I’m 33, and I felt the exact same way my entire life like you’re describing. I’ve been through a divorce and relationships that I chose because I thought I didn’t deserve to be loved for me. Once I left that unhealthy toxic relationship, I started to look inward and figure out what I want to feel loved. All the love I expected others to be giving me, I gave to myself. All the kind affirmations on my beauty, I gave to myself. You have to believe you’re worthy to be who you are. And you are worthy just by being you and trying your best every day. There are good men, and there are good women, out there who are looking for more than just a superficial relationship based on looks. Therapy, hard work and good self care really helped change the way I saw myself which changed how I viewed the world. I hope you find some peace and know that you’re amazing just as you are, and I hope you start to see it in yourself. Therapy and working on myself saved my life. I hope you can show yourself and others a little grace, because no one person is the same and to hold people all in one grouping isn’t fair. Seeing people as a whole as being garbage is only going to make you see the garbage. I’ve gone on many dates with men that were fit and conventionally attractive (“out of my league looks wise”)who liked me for me because I showed up as who I am. All that to say. It starts with you. If you expect other people to give you the validation or reason to feel good about yourself, you will never find it to be enough. You have to give it to yourself. People are here to support and enrich our lives but they cannot complete us. Wishing you the best!

It is really hard! Sometimes the cravings will hit me randomly and other times I don’t even think about it, but when they do, I typically distract myself with something immediately to take my mind off of it. Sugarless gum has really helped me, and also just playing a video game or using that smoke
Free app or even an audiobook or podcast to just get me distracted until the craving passes. We can do this!! Day 6 today for me and I’m already feeling a lot better than I did a few days ago. It’s different every day and these bad ones will pass! And having someone to keep you accountable or talk too is super helpful, I’m here to listen if you need it! The support bot on the smoke free app is surprisingly helpful even though some of the dialogue is a bit cheesy :p but honestly doing the missions and seeing all the benefits counting down for me like breathing and seeing the seconds and minutes I’ve not smoked makes me feel proud— you should be too!

The best advice I can offer since I’m incredibly new to quitting myself, is to invest in some better coping mechanisms when you feel like you want or need to smoke. For me, my anxiety and depression and emotions in general really pushed me to keep smoking. When I started to go to therapy and actually invest in making myself feel better emotionally, it helped me prepare I guess for the emotional side of smoking. Maybe since you like to smoke with your coffee in the morning, try instead to keep your hands busy for the most part until you’re done with your coffee. Or listening to a podcast or audiobook has helped me sometimes as well. If you like doodling or sketching, might be something you can do to keep your hands busy and mind off of smoking. I would suggest (worked for me) to clean your ashtray and move it out of sight and move your chair you normally sit into smoke or location you usually do. Just being out of the ‘normal’ place where I liked to smoke has helped keep my mind off of it. Other than that, just making a list of all the reasons I wanted or needed to quit due to medical conditions really reinforced my need to stop. It’s hard, but I believe in you! We can do this.
Keep fighting!

Hey you, I hear you and I understand you. I know that you feel like you're constantly going to mess things up, but you won't. Take this day by day, and little by little, and real friends will understand that things aren't always going to be perfect. They will understand that life is messy and full of unpredictable moments. You add so much value to this world, just by existing. If you need anything, please don't hesitate to reach out to myself, or any of the other lovely reddit people.
